references.shows: Front, back and side photos of a six-course Renaissance reconstruction show a broad soundboard, the neck joint, a ribbed bowl and a sharply folded pegbox.
The Met traces the development of the Renaissance lute and distinguishes its frets and sharply bent pegbox from the oud.
Neutral side photograph of the 51 cm walnut-bowl model shows the deep curved ribs and pegbox receding from the fingerboard.

silhouette: A full pear-shaped soundboard over a ribbed bowl, with a short tied-fret neck and a narrow pegbox folded sharply backward.
features: Broad, unwaisted pear soundboard with a rounded base and a narrow shoulder at the neck.
Shallow exposure of the ribbed bowl below the near edge.
One carved circular rose between the neck joint and low tied bridge.
Eight tied neck frets and a narrow pegbox angled sharply behind the nut.
Five paired courses and one single treble course, with eleven side pegs.
iconFeatures: Diagonal playing pose with a broad pear body and a short neck.
A compact bend at the pegbox and one carved rose.
avoid: A guitar waist, long mandole neck or flat in-line headstock.
The fretless neck and multiple soundholes of the catalogue oud.
notes: The 51 cm six-course model guides the proportions. The drawing uses a shallow three-quarter angle to show the fold of the pegbox and the near ribs of the bowl.

geometry.view: Shallow soundboard-side three-quarter view in playing orientation
geometry.proportions: The soundboard accounts for about three fifths of the straight length up to the nut. Its width is a little over two thirds of its length.
geometry.partLayout: Center the neck on the soundboard’s narrow shoulder. Place the carved rose on the string axis and the low tied bridge near the broad base. Roll the pegbox behind the nut and stagger the side pegs.

documentedDimensions.scope: Sarah Blanchard six-course soprano lute with nine walnut ribs
